{"kind":"proof","text":"For each \(x\in[0,1)\), \(x^n\to0\), while \(f_n(1)=1\) for every \(n\). Thus the pointwise limit is
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}0,&0\le x<1,\\1,&x=1.\end{cases}
\]
Any uniform limit would necessarily equal this pointwise limit. Fix \(\varepsilon=\tfrac12\). For every \(N\in\mathbb Z_+\), take \(n=N\) and \(x=2^{-1/N}<1\). Then
\[
|f_n(x)-f(x)|=x^n=\left(2^{-1/N}\right)^N=\tfrac12.
\]
Hence for every \(N\) there exist \(n\ge N\) and \(x\in[0,1]\) such that \(|f_n(x)-f(x)|\ge\varepsilon\). {"kind":"proof","text":"Since \(\{0\}\) is closed in \(\mathbb{R}\) and the continuous map \(f:X\to\mathbb{R}\) has closed preimages of closed sets, \(f^{-1}(\{0\})\) is closed in \(X\). Moreover,
\[
Z(f)=\{p\in X:f(p)=0\}=f^{-1}(\{0\}).
\]
Therefore \(Z(f)\) is closed.","reason":"The zero set is the preimage of the closed set \(\{0\}\) under the continuous function \(f\)."}
